kevin: Heads-up — I'm sketching a playbook for canary instrumentation that pulls runtime + infra signals into one comparative dashboard. Need quick cross-team input.
anya: Nice. Which signals are you thinking?
mike: p95/p99 latency per-route, error-rate, cpu/gpu utilization, queue length, plus model-quality deltas (bleu/rouge/semantic-score).
sophia: Also important: request sampling. We can't send full payloads to quality evals for all requests. We should add a deterministic sampler (route + user_id hash) and surface sample rate.
kevin: Agree. Prototype signals list: `route.latency.p95`, `route.latency.p99`, `route.error_rate`, `model.quality.delta`, `node.gpu.util`, `inflight.queue_depth`, `kv_cache.hit_rate`. Want these as pairwise deltas (candidate vs baseline) and absolute baselines.
liz: For dashboards I prefer a split layout: left: candidate vs baseline time series + delta, middle: distribution (CDF) and heatmap by route, right: infra resource flags and sample-rate.
kevin: Sketching queries — PromQL-ish for runtime: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(route_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le,route,model_id))` and for delta: `rate(route_latency_p95{variant=\"candidate\"}[5m]) - rate(route_latency_p95{variant=\"baseline\"}[5m])`. Thoughts?
mike: Works. But we need consistent labels: `route`, `model_id`, `region`, `customer_tier`, `variant`. If those labels aren't present everywhere, joins will be painful.
sophia: Important - telemetry ingestion path differs: infra -> Prometheus; runtime -> OTLP -> ClickHouse. We need a short-term join plan. Either push runtime aggregates into Prom or query both data stores for panels. Grafana can do mixed sources but it complicates alerting.
anke: (typo)
kevin: Re: alerts — let's separate dashboard signals vs alerting signals. Dashboard should be exhaustive; alerts should be lightweight derived signals (p95_delta > threshold AND error_rate_increase > x). Liz, can you propose threshold defaults?
liz: For start: p95_delta > 100ms AND error_rate relative increase > 20% (over 15m). Keep as editable per-route.
anya: Quotas/cost note: model-quality evals are expensive. We should limit sample to 1% by default and provide per-customer overrides. Also retention: keep raw quality scores for 30d then roll up.
mike: Agree on retention. Also add a `telemetry_cost_estimate` metric that we show in the dashboard header (tokens evaluated, compute seconds, est $). Helps PMs see impact of more sampling.
sophia: Security/privacy: quality evals may include PII. Ensure we scrub or use hashed IDs and require opt-in for storing full payloads. Add a toggle in Console per-customer.
kevin: UX ask: in Console rollouts view, add a compact diff row that shows the top 3 regressions and the p95 delta. Clicking expands to full dashboard. This will reduce context switching.
liz: Also add a changelog panel showing which model weights or quantization changed between baseline/candidate (from model registry).
kevin: Implementation plan: 1) finalize metrics list + labels, 2) small schema adapter to push runtime aggregates into Prom for 1:1 comparison, 3) Grafana dashboard + Console iframe, 4) alert rules + Playbook docs. Target: 3 sprints.
man: placeholder
anya: Who owns step 2? We need someone from eng-runtime to own the adapter; mike?
mike: I can own the adapter but will need eng-infra help for Prom write permissions and retention knobs.
sophia: I'll coordinate with security on PII scrub and retention policy.
liz: I'll wire the dashboard layout and thresholds and add the Console panel mock.
kevin: Great. Action items: @mike to open an RFC for the adapter, include label contract; @liz to submit dashboard mock; @sophia to write privacy checklist. Can we meet Wed 11am to align?
anya: Wed 11 works for me.
mike: Put a calendar invite.
canary-bot: Canary run finished — baseline: `r1.4` vs candidate: `r1.5-canary-7`. Key diffs: p95 +120ms on /search, error rate +2.8% on /chat, model.quality.delta -0.03 on semantic-score.
kevin: Thanks bot — we'll triage in the sync.
sophia: Also capture which hosts had KV cache evictions during the canary, that's sometimes the root cause. Add `kv_cache.evictions` to the panel.
mike: noted. I'll include it in the adapter labels.
kevin: Perfect. If anyone has objections to the label set (`route,model_id,variant,region,customer_tier,instance`), raise now; otherwise I'll lock in and start the RFC.
anya: No objections from product side.
liz: LGTM.
kevin: Thanks all — will post RFC link here once created.
